newsitem.title: USA: Blue-chip stocks end lower, dogged by jittery bond market.
newsitem.headline: Blue-chip stocks end lower, dogged by jittery bond market.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks whirled to a lower close on Wednesday as they fell victim to a jittery bond market, despite news that U.S. producer prices in July slid for a record seventh straight month.
The Dow Jones industrial average was off 32.52 points at 7,928.32 after giving back a gain of nearly 80 points.
In the broader market, declining issues led advances 1,463 to 1,358 on heavy volume of 587 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

In the bond market, the benchmark 30-year Treasury bond, which rose more than a full point initially, retreated to end with a gain of only 19/32, and the yield was at 6.63 percent from Tuesday's close of 6.67 percent. Bond prices and yields move in opposite directions.
Stocks started sharply higher on reassuring reports on inflation and retail sales for July, only to track the bond market through a rapid retreat, which in turn, focused on the weak dollar.
Analysts said the dollar's steep slide weighed on financial markets, noting that stocks seemed to have every reason to rally after the latest economic data.

"This morning's numbers were nothing short of phenomenal from the market's perspective," said Phil Orlando, chief investment officer at Value Line Asset Management. "If you were to put a gun to my head and ask for one word that moved the markets today it would be 'currency'."
The dollar ended at 1.8345 German marks, down sharply from 1.8630 marks at Tuesday's close. It also fell to 115.70 Japanese yen from 116.28.

While a weaker dollar over time can lift the earnings of export-oriented U.S. companies, because of beneficial effects on the translation of international sales, it also discourages foreigners from holding dollar-based stocks and bonds.
After watching stocks fail to sustain their early gains, some analysts argued further nervousness may rattle Wall Street.

"I think the ingredients are there for an additional pullback," said Jack Shaughnessy, director of research at Advest. "The volatility we saw was a manifestation of the great deal of indecision that is in the market."

Stocks burst higher from the opening after the government reported that the Producer Price index -- one of the key gauges of inflation -- dropped unexpectedly for a record seventh month in a row in July
The PPI was off 0.1 percent, following an identical drop in June. Without the volatile food and energy components, wholesale prices also fell by 0.1 percent.
Wall Street analysts surveyed by Reuters had expected prices to rise by 0.1 percent last month.
In a separate report, the Commerce Department said July retail sales were up a moderate 0.6 percent last month, reflecting a broadbased improvement in all businesses except furniture.
Economists in a Reuters survey had expected a 0.7 percent rise in overall retail sales.

The reports will be among the data considered by Federal Reserve policy-makers next week when they decide whether economic growth is strong enough to require a rise in interest rates in a pre-emptive move against inflation.

Leading the Dow index lower were oil components Chevron Corp., down 1-13/16 to 79 and Exxon Corp., off 1-3/4 to 60-3/4. Analysts cited concern that Iraq's resumption of oil exports could depress prices and the companies' earnings.
The Nasdaq Composite index rose 7.16 points to 1,583.40, lifted by strong gains among semiconductor equipment makers.
Applied Materials Inc. sparked the rally in the sector, surging 9-1/8 to 99-3/8 after it reported surprisingly strong earnings.
Among individual issues, chip maker Micron Technology Inc. skidded 7-1/2 to 42-5/8 after several investment houses downgraded the stock over worries about memory prices.
Micron was the NYSE's most active issue, with more than 23 million shares changing hands.
Central Sprinkler Corp. fell 1/4 to 19-3/4 on reports that the company's fire-sprinkler head have failed to work properly.
CorporateFamily Solutions Inc. jumped 3-5/8 to 13-5/8 in the company's Wall Street debut after launching its initial public offering. CorporateFamily provides child care at workplace sites.
Boeing Co. rose 1-9/16 to 58-1/16. Smith Barney upgraded the stock based on expected cost savings from the company's merger with McDonnell Douglas Corp.
The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks fell 4.51 points to 922.02. The American Stock Exchange index was off 2.17 to 641.06.
The NYSE Composite index of all listed common stocks fell 2.34 to 478.43. The average share was down 22 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 8,784.770 down 31.132 or 0.35 percent.
